menu_options.nintendo: Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 (Nintendo account, no modification)

ps5.title: PlayStation 5
ps5.description: The console must be on or in rest mode. In rest mode, enable Settings > System > Power Saving > Features Available in Rest Mode > Stay Connected to the Internet and Enable Turning On PS5 from Network.

ps5_pairing.title: Power control
ps5_pairing.description: Turning the PS5 on and off needs a Remote Play pairing. Status works without it.

ps5_import.title: Reuse the PS5-MQTT pairing
ps5_import.description: Reads /config/ps5-mqtt/credentials.json. PS5-MQTT can be uninstalled afterwards.

data.passcode: PSN login passcode (only if the console asks for one)

ps5_register.title: Pair with a PIN
ps5_register.description: On the PS5: Settings > System > Remote Play > Link Device, then enter the 8-digit PIN shown. The account ID is filled in when the PlayStation Network account was linked in the previous step.

data.passcode: PSN login passcode (only if the console asks for one)

ps3.title: PlayStation 3
ps3.description: Requires a console running webMAN MOD (CFW or PS3HEN) and turned on. A PS3 cannot be powered on over the network: link a script in the options (e.g. HDMI-CEC through the TV).

switch.title: Nintendo Switch
switch.description: Requires Switch Assistant on the console (Atmosphère) and the MQTT integration. The client ID is shown in the Switch Assistant app.

switch_confirm.title: Nintendo Switch found
switch_confirm.description: Switch Assistant client {client_id} publishes on MQTT. Add it to Gaming Hub?

psn.title: PlayStation Network account (optional)
psn.description: Gives the current game with its artwork, the online status, trophies and PlayStation Plus, without any other integration. Sign in on playstation.com, open {npsso_url} and copy the value of "npsso". Leave empty to skip.

reauth_confirm.title: PlayStation Network token expired
reauth_confirm.description: The NPSSO token lasts about two months. Sign in on playstation.com, open {npsso_url} and copy the new value of "npsso".

nintendo.title: Nintendo account
nintendo.description:
Sign in with the Nintendo account that manages the console in the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app (the console must be linked to it). Open the [Nintendo sign-in]({login_url}), sign in, then right-click the red button of the account (long press on a phone), choose **Copy link** and paste it below.

Nintendo gives the games and the play time with a delay, never whether the console is on, and does not allow turning it on or off: the hub counts the console on while its play time grows.

nintendo_console.title: Console
nintendo_console.description: This Nintendo account manages several consoles.

nintendo_reauth.title: Nintendo account signed out
nintendo_reauth.description: Nintendo refused the session (signed out, password changed…). Open the [Nintendo sign-in]({login_url}), sign in, then right-click the red button of the account (long press on a phone), choose **Copy link** and paste it below.

steam.title: Steam account
steam.description:
Gaming Hub reads the account's status and the game being played through Steam's official API, for a PC, a Steam Deck or anything running Steam.

1. Create a key on [Steam's key page]({key_url}) while signed in to the account (any domain name, e.g. homeassistant.local). Steam may ask to confirm in the Steam mobile app.
2. In the Steam profile, Privacy settings → Game details: **Public**, or the game is not reported.

data_description.account: Profile link (steamcommunity.com/id/… or /profiles/…), custom profile name or SteamID64.

steam_reauth.title: Steam key refused
steam_reauth.description: Steam refused the Web API key (revoked or replaced). Create a new one on [Steam's key page]({key_url}).

playstation.title: PS4 or PS3 through the PlayStation Network
playstation.description:
Gaming Hub follows the console through its PlayStation Network account: on while the account is online on it, with the game being played. The console must sign in to the PlayStation Network when it starts. No power on or off.

Sign in on playstation.com, open {npsso_url} and copy the value of "npsso".

init.title: Options

data_description.power_entity: A smart plug powering the console: the Power and Energy sensors only exist with it.
data_description.turn_on_entity: Script, button or switch turning the console on.
data_description.turn_off_entity: Script, button or switch turning the console off.
data_description.block_entity: Activated instead of turning the console off when play time is over.
data_description.state_entity: An entity telling whether the console is on: a switch powering the computer, a ping, an HDMI input, a smart plug's power (on above 5 W)… It decides on or off; the console or its account still gives the game.
data_description.restart_entity: Script or button restarting the console.

init.description: Only what this console cannot do by itself is offered: an entity of yours fills it in. A switch chosen as state also turns the console on and off.

energy.title: Existing consumption
energy.description: The console now has its own Power and Energy sensors. If the plug, or a helper built on it, already has an energy meter, pick it here: its history moves to the console's Energy sensor, which also replaces it on the Energy dashboard, so nothing is counted twice. Leave empty to take nothing over.

data.hide_sources: Hide the plug's sensors and the meter taken over

data_description.energy_source: The history is moved, not copied: the meter taken over goes on alone, without its past.
data_description.hide_sources: They show again when the plug is unlinked or the console deleted.

unsupported.message: This console does not support {command}. Link a script or switch in the options.

command_failed.message: The console did not accept the command: {reason}.

removed_kind.message: Gaming Hub no longer follows another integration's entity: everything goes through Gaming Hub. Delete this console and add it again with a supported type.

user.title: Profile
user.description: A child (or anyone) whose play time is counted across the consoles. Their time comes from their accounts and Switch players; the rest of a console's time goes to its main player.

data_description.accounts: Steam accounts, and PlayStation Network accounts linked to a console: their play counts for this profile.
data_description.players: Users of a Switch followed through the Nintendo account.
data_description.consoles: Time no account or player accounts for goes to this profile.
